title: Re-found broker completion on Job-empty so drained() cannot deadlock on the broker's own pipe copies
description:
Successor to task-7ba898f5 (nonblocking control polling), split out by governor ruling 2026-08-16 01:00Z with the human's standing unblock authorization. worker-dd806f63's measured findings (Serena: gotcha-broker-completed-is-gated-on-parent-teardown, task-task-7ba898f5...-handoff):

THE DEADLOCK. packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/src/settle.rs:113-123 `fn drained<B: ByteChannel>` calls blocking `channel.read(&mut scratch)` and returns true only on `Ok(0)`; settle.rs:88-98 gates `Completion::Completed` on BOTH stdout/stderr drains, else `Completion::Unknown(Unobserved::ProviderEof)`. On a real Windows stdio pipe the broker holds its own fd4/fd5 write-end copies, so child exit never produces EOF — EOF arrives only when the NODE PARENT closes its endpoint (windows-boundary-session.ts:183-198 via windows-broker-process.ts:99-103, cancel/timeout/close only; onCompleted passes closeChannels=false). Measured: child gone ~200ms, boundary.completed at ~timeoutMs (6017ms for 6000, ~2000 for 2000). Through launchClaude, boundary-cancel and launcher-TIMEOUT coincide, closeProviderChannels destroys both captures, and the public result is CLAUDE_LAUNCH_STREAM_ERROR@OUTPUT.

REQUIRED DIRECTION (worker-validated; both naive halves fail alone): re-found the drain precondition on `wait_until_job_is_empty` — the Job-empty proof already guarantees zero live processes can hold a write end, so the post-Job-empty drain is bounded. Merely swapping drained() to poll_read yields Pending forever; merely closing the broker's fd copies after CreateProcess makes the broker's own drain unreadable. A never-ending provider must STILL reach Unobserved::ProviderEof. This is a semantic change to the completion contract — the architect must plan it as such, including which of settle.rs / session.rs / completion.rs it owns.

ACCEPTANCE ANCHOR: with this landed plus 7ba's delivered polling layer, the public launcher returns PROVEN (not TIMEOUT-coupled STREAM_ERROR) for a provider that outlives the 50ms slice and exits naturally, completion time tracking the CHILD (~hundreds of ms), not the configured timeout. The formerly-red untracked claude-launcher.windows.test.ts case "stays alive beyond the control poll slice" is the live repro — adopt or supersede it explicitly.

Task-7ba898f5 completes independently on its fd0/polling half; its DoD 1 natural-exit-PROVEN clause is explicitly re-scoped HERE (recorded in 7ba's status reason). task-6cbff010's Windows prerequisite chain is satisfied only when BOTH tasks are DONE — its architect must name both ids at re-measurement.
definitionOfDone: A real-Windows test proves the public launcher returns PROVEN for a provider that outlives the 50ms slice and exits naturally, with completion latency bounded by child exit (assert an explicit literal bound well under the configured timeout), not by timeoutMs.
A never-ending provider still reaches Unobserved::ProviderEof / its mapped stable refusal — the re-founding must not convert the old deadlock into a hang or a fail-open success.

The drain precondition is anchored on the Job-empty proof: a test (or drill) shows the drain runs only after wait_until_job_is_empty succeeds, and a mutation restoring the blocking pre-Job-empty drain turns a NAMED test red.
The formerly-red claude-launcher.windows.test.ts repro case ("stays alive beyond the control poll slice") is green, adopted into tracked tests or explicitly superseded by an equivalent named case.
Broker suite stays green on real Windows with nonzero executed counts; each gate leg's exit code read separately; foreign red disclosed verbatim under the path-attributed baseline rail.
